description:
You are a biostatistician at an oncology research center analyzing data from the German Breast Cancer Study Group (GBSG) randomized trial. The dataset is the GBSG2 data from the TH.data R package, containing 686 patients with primary node-positive breast cancer who were followed for recurrence or death.

Your complete analysis must produce four deliverables:

1. Fit a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model with the following covariates: hormonal therapy (horTh), tumor size (tsize), number of positive nodes (pnodes), progesterone receptor level (progrec), estrogen receptor level (estrec), menopausal status (menostat), and tumor grade (tgrade). Write the Cox model summary to /home/ga/RProjects/output/gbsg_cox_results.csv with columns: covariate, hazard_ratio, hr_lower95, hr_upper95, p_value, significant (TRUE/FALSE at alpha=0.05).

2. Test the proportional hazards assumption using cox.zph(). Write the test results to /home/ga/RProjects/output/gbsg_ph_test.csv with columns: covariate, chisq, df, p_value, ph_violated (TRUE if p < 0.05). Identify which covariates violate the PH assumption and note them.

3. Generate Kaplan-Meier survival curves stratified by hormonal therapy (horTh: yes vs no) with a risk table below the plot. Use the survminer package (ggsurvplot). The plot must show: survival probability on y-axis, time in days on x-axis, number-at-risk table, and log-rank test p-value. Save to /home/ga/RProjects/output/gbsg_km_curves.png.

4. Generate a forest plot of hazard ratios for all covariates from the Cox model. Each row should show: covariate name, HR estimate, and 95% CI bar. Save to /home/ga/RProjects/output/gbsg_forest_plot.png.

Login: username=ga, password=password123. RStudio is open. Write your code in /home/ga/RProjects/survival_analysis.R.
